item.title: [Recap] Kyshawn George (WAS): Kyshawn George had himself a night with 33 points (10-of-20 FGs, 8-of-10 FTs), four rebounds, seven assists, a steal, two blocks and five 3-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Hawks.
item.description:
Kyshawn George had himself a night with 33 points (10-of-20 FGs, 8-of-10 FTs), four rebounds, seven assists, a steal, two blocks and five 3-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Hawks.

Another great game from Kyshawn George who led the team in shot attempts (Check). He was one point away from his career high. (check)He made a lot of winning plays and was a big reason the Wizards stayed in this game, especially in the fourth quarter. He’s been awesome this season and while Anthony Davis was out in this one, he consistently shows up and gets things done. He won’t continue at the level he has been playing at recently, but he’s a very good player. If you have him, it might be worth exploring the market and see if there’s a sell high available.

Brian Taylor

item.title: [Recap] Trae Young (WAS): Trae Young had 23 points (7-of-16 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), two rebounds, ten assists, a steal, three 3-pointers and eight turnovers in a 139-132 loss to the Hawks on Friday.
item.description:
Trae Young had 23 points (7-of-16 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), two rebounds, ten assists, a steal, three 3-pointers and eight turnovers in a 139-132 loss to the Hawks on Friday.

At the end of the game, he hurt his left elbow as he fell to the ground which will be something to monitor. It could be a funny bone, but it’s possible he shows up on the injury report. He finished the game which is a positive sign. In his return to Atlanta, he did his best to lead the Wizards to a win, but to no avail. The league leader in assists continues to be very consistent on that front. It’s not great he had 8 turnovers which left a mark in the turnovers category.

item.description:

His fantasy game is very empty outside of the scoring and 3’s which limits his fantasy upside, but he is a really good shooter. If AD misses another game, you can consider a stream of Tre Johnson if you’re in need of the points and 3’s. He’s much better in points leagues than category leagues.

item.description:

item.title: [Recap] Luguentz Dort (ATL): Luguentz Dort put up 25 points (9-of-15 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), seven rebounds, four assists, two steals and five 3-pointers in Friday’s win over the Wizards.
item.description:
Luguentz Dort put up 25 points (9-of-15 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), seven rebounds, four assists, two steals and five 3-pointers in Friday’s win over the Wizards.

Dort hasn’t had the same role that he had with Oklahoma City, but it was a good game in this one. He’s having a similar output to last season in terms of efficiency, which isn’t great since he’s been below 40% from the field. He has been impactful on defense and has value there. He’s still a deeper league guy despite having a good performance. He has been notorious for being volatile in terms of his day-to-day performances. He’s worth a stream in start while keeping in mind that he might ruin your FG% category.

item.title: [Recap] Jayson Tatum (BOS): Jayson Tatum accumulated a game-high 34 points (9-of-16 FGs, 11-of-11 FTs), eight rebounds, nine assists, one steal and one block in 29 minutes, leading the Celtics to a 119-80 blowout win over the Hornets on Friday.
item.description:
Jayson Tatum accumulated a game-high 34 points (9-of-16 FGs, 11-of-11 FTs), eight rebounds, nine assists, one steal and one block in 29 minutes, leading the Celtics to a 119-80 blowout win over the Hornets on Friday.

Simply put, Tatum loves playing in North Carolina. The 28-year-old franchise cornerstone reached the 30-point plateau with a nifty reverse layup midway through the third quarter as Boston continued pulling away, eventually opening up a near 40-point lead by the end of the third quarter. He put the finishing touch on his monster evening by knocking down his 11th free throw of the night in the final minute of the quarter, finishing just shy of a triple-double in a monster statsheet-stuffing effort. The lopsided score allowed him to sit out the fourth, otherwise he may have been in line for an even bigger performance. He’s delivered top-30 fantasy value in the early stages of the season, recording four 30-point efforts in his first eight games. The Celtics close out the week with a road tilt against the Bucks on Sunday before kicking off a three-game week with road matchups against the 76ers and Raptors.

George Bissell

item.title: [Recap] Naz Reid (CHA): Naz Reid tallied 14 points (6-of-17 FGs), six rebounds, two assists and one steal over 26 minutes in a blowout loss to the Celtics on Friday.
item.description:
Naz Reid tallied 14 points (6-of-17 FGs), six rebounds, two assists and one steal over 26 minutes in a blowout loss to the Celtics on Friday.

There weren’t a ton of bright spots for the Hornets as they failed to eclipse 91 points for the fourth time in 10 games to open this season. Boston raced out to a massive 70-39 advantage by halftime and never really looked back. Coming off a season-high 28-point effort against the Nets earlier this week, Reid drew the start in place of an injured Moussa Diabaté (quad) in this one and led Charlotte with 17 shot attempts. He’s shown some signs of life recently after a rough start to his Hornets debut.

George Bissell

item.title: [Recap] Stephen Curry (GSW): Stephen Curry led the Warriors with 29 points (9-of-19 FGs), one rebound, four assists, one steal and six three-pointers in a 120-100 win over the Heat on Thursday.
item.description:
Stephen Curry led the Warriors with 29 points (9-of-19 FGs), one rebound, four assists, one steal and six three-pointers in a 120-100 win over the Heat on Thursday.

Despite a rough start to this game, Curry got going in the third quarter. After scoring seven points on 2-of-10 shooting in the first half, he scored 14 points in the third quarter alone and eight more points in the fourth to steal the win for Golden State. Curry has been unbelievable to start the season, which has him ranked as one of the best players in fantasy basketball to this point. He’ll look to stay hot against the Magic to wrap up the week on Saturday.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] Yaxel Lendeborg (GSW): Yaxel Lendeborg posted a full line on Thursday with 17 points (6-of-14 FGs), eight rebounds, six assists, three steals, one block and one three-pointer against the Heat.
item.description:
Yaxel Lendeborg posted a full line on Thursday with 17 points (6-of-14 FGs), eight rebounds, six assists, three steals, one block and one three-pointer against the Heat.

Lendeborg has been one of the best rookies in the league this season, which has worked out well for fantasy managers, especially as of late. Since he was held to six points against the Lakers last week, he has averaged 23.3 points,5.7 rebounds, 5.7 assists, 1.7 steals and 3.0 triples per game. Lendeborg has been able to make an impact on both ends of the floor, with his only weakness in fantasy basketball being too many turnovers.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] Davion Mitchell (MIA): Davion Mitchell led the Heat with 22 points (9-of-18 FGs), two rebounds, eight assists, one steal, four three-pointers and five turnovers in a 120-100 loss to the Warriors on Thursday.
item.description:
Davion Mitchell led the Heat with 22 points (9-of-18 FGs), two rebounds, eight assists, one steal, four three-pointers and five turnovers in a 120-100 loss to the Warriors on Thursday.

Mitchell’s breakout season continued in this game as he matched his season high for both points and three-pointers. His assists continue to be the strongest aspect of his game, but he is averaging career highs for points, triples and steals as well while also posting the best shooting percentage of his career. It has been a rough start to the year for Miami, but Mitchell has been able to thrive regardless.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] Devin Booker (PHX): Devin Booker led the Suns with 30 points (11-of-22 FGs), one rebound, eight assists, three steals and four three-pointers in a 117-104 win over the Magic on Thursday.
item.description:
Devin Booker led the Suns with 30 points (11-of-22 FGs), one rebound, eight assists, three steals and four three-pointers in a 117-104 win over the Magic on Thursday.

Booker has had a few rough performances early on this season, but this has been an excellent two-game stretch for him. He has scored at least 30 points in back-to-back games, and he set a new season high for assists, steals and three-pointers in this one. Outside of a dud game against the Thunder, Booker has been excellent this season. item.description:

After playing 22 minutes in his first start of the season on Monday, Lopez played 35 in Wednesday’s overtime thriller. Given his production in those two starts and Isaiah Jackson’s inability to avoid silly fouls, Lopez may have the starting center job for the foreseeable future. Jackson, who has committed at least four fouls in six of his eight games, played 13 minutes against the Heat and finished with two points, four rebounds, two assists and one steal.

In addition to making 10 of 14 shots from the field, he recorded seven assists, making for a decent night at the office.

item.title: [Recap] Rui Hachimura (LAC): Rui Hachimura accumulated 21 points (7-of-18 FGs, 6-of-7 FTs), nine rebounds, seven assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s loss to the Heat.
item.description:
Rui Hachimura accumulated 21 points (7-of-18 FGs, 6-of-7 FTs), nine rebounds, seven assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s loss to the Heat.

Hachimura has gotten off to a relatively slow start with the Clippers, shooting 37.3 percent from the field and 68.4 percent from the foul line. Add inconsistent production in assists, steals and blocks, and rostering Hachimura in some 10-team leagues isn’t worth discussing. He had a productive night against the Heat, with the seven assists being more than double his total entering the night (three). For Hachimura to be someone you can roster in shallow leagues after the Clippers get guys like Brandon Ingram and Bradley Beal back, nights like Wednesday have to become the norm.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Giannis Antetokounmpo (MIA): Giannis Antetokounmpo recorded 27 points (8-of-20 FGs, 11-of-13 FTs), 14 rebounds, six assists, two steals and three blocks in Wednesday’s win over the Clippers.
item.description:

The opposite happened against the Clippers, with the Heat forward shooting 40 percent from the field and 84.6 percent from the foul line. item.description:

item.title: [Recap] Bam Adebayo (MIA): Bam Adebayo recorded 35 points (14-of-20 FGs, 6-of-8 FTs), 10 rebounds, four assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s win over the Clippers.
item.description:

Add in the assists, and it was a good night for those rostering the Heat captain. Even with there still being some bumps the Heat need to smooth over as they work Giannis Antetokounmpo into the fold, Adebayo has been close to a top-25 player in 12-team leagues. That’s encouraging, to say the least.

item.description:

The second-year wing had the best night of his NBA career, dropping a career-high 26 points. Sanders scored 13 points in both halves, but he may have run out of steam late. Shooting 1-of-5 from the field, Sanders scored five points in the fourth quarter, and the Clippers shot 30.4 percent as a team. That’s how a team goes from leading by 13 to losing by seven.
